assertion.text: Erdős Problem #812: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. Is it true that\[\frac{R(n+1)}{R(n)}\geq 1+c\]for some constant $c>0$, for all large $n$? Is it true that\[R(n+1)-R(n) \gg n^2?\] Current best: Burr, Erd\H{o}s, Faudree, and Schelp \cite{BEFS89} proved that\[R(n+1)-R(n) \geq 4n-8\]for all $n\geq 2$. The lower bound of [165] implies that\[R(n+2)-R(n) \gg n^{2-o(1)}.\]  References  [BEFS89] Burr, S. Prize: no. OEIS: A059442. Tags: graph theory, ramsey theory.
